summary:
El Hadji Diouf is a Senegalese former forward whose standout 2002 World Cup helped launch a high-profile career in European football. Senegal reached the quarter-finals, beating defending champions France, and Diouf was named to the tournament’s All-Star team.

After starting in France, he joined Liverpool in 2002 but struggled to score and left for Bolton, where he became a fan favourite. He later played for Sunderland, Blackburn Rovers, Rangers, Doncaster Rovers, Leeds United and Sabah in Malaysia.

Diouf earned 69 caps and scored 21 goals for Senegal. He also helped the team reach the 2002 African Cup of Nations final and was named African Footballer of the Year twice. His career was frequently marked by disciplinary trouble, including spitting incidents that led to fines, bans and a criminal charge. He was also included in FIFA’s 2004 list of 125 greatest living footballers.
